absent: Locking, lifetime, and concurrency rules for swap descriptor, extent tree, and activation versus teardown
Allocation, initialization, and queuing behavior of swap IO context and the disk queueing routine
Full layouts of swap extent, swap cluster info, swap info, and swap IO control block
Numeric values of swap flags, cluster sizes, page and sector shifts, and error codes beyond invalid, memory exhaustion, not found, and IO error
Compressed store entry, pool, and tree structures, eviction, and accounting beyond load and swapin paths
Zsmalloc pool, size class, zspage, handle encoding, and migration interaction beyond read pinning
Page owner query, display, deallocation tracking, and stack depot interfaces
Early page tagging in populated zones and zone iteration details
Memory stall, delay accounting, pressure stall, and event counter semantics
Device selection between block and filesystem paths and retry policy after IO errors

findings.text: Swap file activation builds a disk extent map by walking file size in page sized block groups, consulting block mapping for each group, accepting only groups that are aligned and contiguous on disk, recording accepted groups through extent insertion, tracking minimum and maximum data positions excluding the header page, deriving span from those bounds, updating device limits and counts, and returning the number of extents created.

Activation treats unmapped or failing block lookups as holes and fails the whole operation with an invalid argument error after logging; misaligned or discontiguous probes advance by a single block and retry; when no usable page is found the limit is forced to one to signal emptiness.

Extent insertion appends a page range at the rightmost position of a balanced tree under the assumption that callers arrive in increasing page order, merging with the predecessor when disk blocks are contiguous and otherwise allocating and balancing a new node, reporting merge versus new node versus allocation exhaustion distinctly.
Callers must present ranges with no gaps and no overlap, where each start equals the prior end; violation is treated as a fatal consistency error rather than a repairable failure.

Merging of folio write requests is gated by memory control charging in one build and ungated in the alternate build; the gated build denies merging when charging states differ and otherwise compares IO control states associated with the folios, while the alternate build always permits merging and performs no association work.

Derivation and comparison of IO control state from folio memory control, and acquisition of a reference for bio association, occur within read side critical sections; the association path drops the reference after linking and handles missing references or uncharged folios by doing nothing further.

Swap IO control block recycling pool is created lazily on first initialization with capacity for a full cluster, published with an atomic compare exchange so concurrent initializers converge on a single instance while losers are destroyed, and initialization reports exhaustion when no pool exists.

Zero map batching measures the length of the initial run of identical zero indications starting at the cluster offset of a swap entry, bounded by the caller supplied maximum and the cluster size, under a read side section, optionally reporting the common value to the caller.
Zero indication for a cluster slot comes from either a flag bit inside a table word when that capability is compiled in, with a check that the word is countable, or from a bitmap otherwise.

Folio swap in requires a locked folio that is not yet valid and either cached or on a synchronous device; working set folios accrue stall and delay accounting around the whole path; a zero map hit completes synchronously with zeroing and validation, otherwise a compressed store hit completes, otherwise disk protection is incremented and the folio is queued for device read.
Large folios that are only partially covered by a uniform zero run are not handled; the path completes without marking validity so upper layers surface an IO error.

Compressed store load looks up the per type tree at the swap offset, returning not found when the feature was never enabled or no entry exists, rejecting large folios, and on decompression failure reporting an IO error; success validates and dirties the folio, removes the tree entry, frees the compressed record, and unlocks.

Decompression serializes per processor cryptographic context with a mutex across scatter setup and teardown; objects whose stored length equals a full page are copied directly with cache maintenance, otherwise assisted decompression fills the folio; only a successful operation producing a full page counts as success, otherwise a failure counter increments with a ratelimited alert.

Stored object read begins by holding the pool read lock to resolve a handle to its location and pinning the containing zspage with a read lock before releasing the pool lock, so migration cannot move pages during the read; the matching end call re resolves the handle and releases the zspage lock.

Read setup describes the object as one scatter segment when it fits within a single page after accounting for handle reservation on non huge pages, otherwise as two segments split at the page boundary using the following page; every begin must be paired with an end.

Write completion walks the vectors of a control block, marking pages dirty and clearing reclaim eligibility on failure while always ending writeback, then recycles the control block; block and filesystem variants differ in failure detection from status versus short length and in alert detail including device identity or file position.

Read completion marks folios valid and accounts events only on success, always unlocks every folio, accounts total length once on success, recycles the control block, and emits ratelimited alerts on failure with device detail for block IO.

Block submit paths initialize a bio over the control block vectors for swap write or plain read, sized and positioned from the first folio sector, associating IO control on write; synchronous devices wait and complete inline, with reads additionally pinning the current task, while asynchronous devices install an end handler and submit.

On disk sector for a folio is its extent start plus its displacement within that extent, expressed in sector units; filesystem offset for a swap entry is its swap offset expressed in byte position units.

Block merging requires sector adjacency between the current folio and the end of the previous folio plus IO control compatibility on writes; filesystem merging requires file position adjacency using swap offsets and prior size.

Block operations table binds write submit, read submit, and merge predicates; filesystem request preparation initializes a synchronous control at the first folio swap position, selects completion by direction, and builds a vector iterator; filesystem activation stores operations and inserts a single extent covering the full range from zero.

Page owner tracking record holds allocation order, last migration reason, allocation mask, allocation and free stack handles, allocation and free timestamps, command name, and process and thread identifiers for both allocation and free.
Stack capture depth is 16; stack print selection bits are 0x1 for stack, 0x2 for pages, and 0x4 for handle.

Stack list node links a depot record and a successor; print context pairs a stack pointer with flag bits; print mode enumerates stack, handle, and combined forms with matching name strings; filter state pairs a print mode with a node mask and an enable flag.
Stack list is guarded by a dedicated spinlock; a per task in tracking flag is set on entry and cleared on exit to suppress recursion when tracking itself allocates.

Early boot option parses a boolean to enable tracking and requests early stack storage; when enabled, initialization captures dummy, failure, and early stacks, tags pages already allocated in each populated zone, pins dummy and failure records, links them as the initial list, and enables the tracking static key.

Disk swap ins increment a per memory group disk counter under a read side section when a folio is present; the never enabled predicate reflects whether the compressed store static branch was ever enabled, honoring its default configuration.

Synchronous block reads pin the submitting task across the wait so out of memory handling can safely inspect it; IO error alerts are ratelimited and do not themselves retry or recover the failed folio beyond normal completion handling.
Page isolation compilation unit requests instantiation of its trace points.
Filesystem swap position is swap offset shifted by page size bits; block sector is extent block position shifted by page size bits minus sector size bits.
